Updated assessment incorporating SLOOS:
- Core FOMC read remains positive: strong labor market and solid activity with inflation expected to move toward 2%, supporting gradual hikes.
- SLOOS nuance: Banks reported broadly unchanged to slightly easier C&I standards for larger firms (credit still available to support capex), but continued tightening in CRE and consumer segments (notably autos/credit cards) with softer demand in several categories; mortgage standards little changed with mixed demand. Net, credit supply is supportive for businesses but shows emerging headwinds for consumer-driven activity and CRE.
- Combined with the FSR’s elevated valuations and leverage, the SLOOS suggests somewhat greater downside sensitivity if financial conditions tighten.

Net: still cautiously hawkish, but a touch more guarded than the FSR-only read given pockets of tightening and softer demand in SLOOS.
